attributes.action: Review the ban on imports of raw-milk cheese imposed due to lumpy skin disease
attributes.additional_details: Lumpy skin disease affects cattle and poses no food safety risk to people. Current restrictions prevent imports of French raw cow's milk cheeses, while heat-treated cheeses can be imported. We believe restricting matured raw-milk cheese intended for human consumption is disproportionate unless evidence shows it presents a credible transmission risk to UK cattle. We ask the Government to review and publish its risk assessment and permit imports where appropriate biosecurity requirements are met.
attributes.background: We want the Government to review the current restrictions on imports of raw cow's milk cheese from France and introduce a proportionate, evidence-based exemption for cheeses intended for human consumption where they do not present a credible risk of transmitting lumpy skin disease to UK livestock.

rejection.details:
Defra has recently revoked lumpy skin disease restrictions for France. 

Details can be found on the following gov.uk pages: 

https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/official-veterinary-surgeon-ovs-notes/27-october-2026-revocation-of-lumpy-skin-disease-restrictions-for-france

https://www.gov.uk/guidance/imports-exports-and-eu-trade-of-animals-and-animal-products-topical-issues#lumpy-skin-disease-in-the-european-union

Defra's update states that "Defra has reviewed the actions taken by the French Competent Authority in response to their previous outbreaks of lumpy skin disease (LSD) and that, as a result, import restrictions on the following commodities from France have been lifted:

live ungulates
fresh meat of ungulates
raw milk and raw milk products
bovine embryos
bovine semen
certain animal by-products, including hides and skins, that were included in the LSD Declaration of Special Measures of 26 June 2025".

It also states "The import restrictions on affected commodities from France have been lifted. This means the export of previously restricted commodities from France can take place, provided that all other import conditions are met and attestations in the relevant export health certificate can be certified. Amendments have been made to the relevant lists of EU and EFTA countries approved to export animals and animal products to Great Britain and the certain ABPs safeguard measures, accordingly."
